fonds: Fondo África → Alta Comisaría de España en Marruecos, 4,990 cajas, 1750–1979 (classification 1.2.5.1, Órganos Centrales). Catalogued in PARES.
holdings: The administrative record of the Spanish protectorate: political files, intelligence, the northern parties, the Khalifate at Tetouan.
whatItCanSettle: The Rif war; northern nationalism and how far Spain sponsored it; Abd el-Krim's own official output before 1915; the Jebala and Raisuni.
access: Reading room; PARES catalogue online.

fonds: GR 3H — Maroc, c. 3,000 articles, 1877–1960 (item inventory 1836–1963). Commandement Supérieur 3H 314–752. Goums 3H 2375–2711. Ministerial telegrams in série N at 5N 39–64. Marine series for the 1907 bombardment.
holdings: The French military and Affaires Indigènes record: operations, intelligence, tribal political reports, personnel.
whatItCanSettle: El Herri and the Khénifra command chain; the 1920 Zaian submission terms; the 'submit or starve' blockade; Bougafer 1933; Franco-Spanish liaison in 1925–26 and the chemical-weapons question on the French side.
access: Reading room, Vincennes. Published inventories.

fonds: FO 413 — Confidential Print Morocco and North West Africa, 1839–1969, 150 volumes, open (catalogue-verified; covers Morocco throughout, extended to Algeria and Tunisia from 1952). FO 174 — Consulate, Tangier. FO 99 — Morocco general correspondence (pre-1906 series). FO 371 — political departments from 1906. Also Admiralty and War Office series.
holdings: British consular, diplomatic and intelligence reporting on Morocco. Britain was the third party in Morocco until it traded its position away in the 1904 Entente, and it kept reporting afterwards.
whatItCanSettle: The independent check on almost every Franco-Spanish claim in this workspace. FO 413 in particular is a curated, printed, chronological digest of British reporting on Morocco across 130 years — the single most efficient entry point to third-party evidence on Casablanca 1907, Annual 1921, the Rif Republic, the Maclean ransom and the 1953 deposition. Confidential Print includes the Foreign Office's own 'descriptions of leading personalities' — i.e. British pen-portraits of the same men French and Spanish intelligence were profiling, which allows direct comparison of three states' assessments of one person.
access: Free reader's ticket; Discovery catalogue online. Some series digitised.

city: Rabat — Avenue Ibn Battouta, near Bab Rouah
fonds: Fonds Protectorat, organised by Protectorate office; cartons with variable levels of description. Pre- and post-Protectorate material also held.
holdings: Roughly 40% of the colonial administrative archive that remained in Morocco at independence — the other 60% went to France. Administrative files, colonial economy, public works.
whatItCanSettle: The Moroccan-held share of the Protectorate record. Crucially, it is the likeliest home in Morocco of the Arabic instrument of the Treaty of Fez and of the 1953 ben Arafa bay'a.
access: Mon-Fri 09:00-16:00, closed August and government holidays. Three-day temporary permit; reader card requires two passport photos, a letter of attestation and ID. Doctoral students c. 100 MAD. Photography permitted free with an authorisation slip. Not wheelchair accessible.

fonds: Weltkrieg files — WK Nr. 11 series cited by Odile Moreau for the Morocco operation. Pre-war Marokko files for the 1905 and 1911 crises.
holdings: German diplomatic and subversion records: the Tangier crisis of 1905, the Agadir crisis of 1911 and the Franco-German convention of 4 November 1911, and the wartime Madrid channel financing and arming Moroccan resistance.
whatItCanSettle: The financing figures currently repeated on thin authority — the '600,000 pesetas per month' and '300,000 marks'. The terms Moulay Abdelhafid actually demanded in Barcelona in 1915. And Hugo Stoltzenberg's chemical supply chain to Spain.
access: Reading room, Berlin.

institution: US National Archives (NARA) — RG 84, Foreign Service Posts
fonds: RG 84 — Records of the Foreign Service Posts. Diplomatic posts: Morocco, 1905–1957. Consular posts: Morocco, 1795–1957. Also Spanish Morocco, 1942–1944.
holdings: Post-level correspondence of the American Legation at Tangier and the consulates. The 1795 start date reflects the Moroccan-American treaty of 1786 — the oldest unbroken US treaty relationship.
whatItCanSettle: The Perdicaris affair of 1904 from the American side; the Anfa conference and its aftermath; American reporting on the nationalist movement, which was courted by Istiqlal precisely because Washington was not a colonial power in Morocco. The Spanish Morocco series (1942–44) is a rare American window on the Spanish zone.
access: Public. Some visa and personnel files require State Department consultation.

fonds: HR.SYS. (Hariciye Siyasi — Foreign Ministry political). DH.KMS. (Interior, Kalem-i Mahsus). DH.MKT. (Interior correspondence). BEO (Bab-ı Ali Evrak Odası). İ.HB. (İrade Harbiye).
holdings: The Ottoman record of the Teşkilât-ı Mahsusa operation in Morocco: officer despatches, Enver Pasha's directives, Madrid legation traffic, negotiations with Moulay Abdelhafid.
whatItCanSettle: This is the workspace's first source of document-level references. Named scholars cite specifically: HR.SYS. 2392/2, 2393/1, 2393/2, 2393/4, D.2109 G.10, D.2392 G.5, D.2393 G.1-3; DH.KMS. 29-28; DH.MKT. 2885-31; BEO 1993-149432 and 4135-310078. These would establish the Ottoman-Moroccan relationship independently of both French and German reporting.
access: Reading room in Istanbul; catalogue searchable on site. The 2013 move to the new building disrupted some access.

fonds: Digitised books, periodicals, press, maps, photographs.
holdings: The French press day by day — Le Temps, L'Illustration, Le Petit Journal — plus colonial-era monographs, the Archives berbères, Bulletin Officiel, and Protectorate ethnography.
whatItCanSettle: Contemporary French framing of Casablanca 1907, El Herri 1914 and the Rif war, as published rather than as later rationalised. Also the Affaires Indigènes scholarly corpus — the richest surviving description of rural Moroccan society, produced in order to govern it.
access: Free and fully online.

fonds: Official Makhzen correspondence. Published document series al-Wathā'iq ('The Archives'), issued from 1976.
holdings: Makhzen correspondence with a focus on pre-colonial Moroccan international relations — i.e. the Moroccan state's own diplomatic record.
whatItCanSettle: The single largest gap in this workspace. Whether Moroccan sovereignty over the Sahara was asserted before or in reaction to European encroachment; the Makhzen's own account of the treaties of 1844, 1860, 1880 and 1906. The published al-Wathā'iq volumes are the accessible entry point and require no reading-room access.
access: Restricted; a public electronic portal has been announced but not confirmed as live. The published volumes circulate in research libraries.

institution: Hemeroteca Digital — Biblioteca Nacional de España
fonds: Digitised Spanish newspapers and periodicals.
holdings: The Spanish press, day by day — including the coverage of the 1909 Melilla campaign that produced the Semana Trágica, and of Annual in 1921.
whatItCanSettle: How the disasters were reported in real time before the official accounts were settled; the political construction of the responsibilities crisis; the range of casualty figures in circulation in 1921 as against those fixed later.
access: Free and fully online.

institution: Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS)
city: Published — Office of the Historian, Department of State
fonds: Annual and conference volumes. The Conferences at Washington and Casablanca, 1941–1943 is the relevant conference volume for Anfa.
coveringDates: Nineteenth century to the recent past
holdings: The official published documentary record of US foreign policy: cables, memoranda of conversation, position papers.
whatItCanSettle: Anfa, 22 January 1943. This workspace previously recorded 'what Roosevelt said' as unknown. Stenner (2014) works from State Department records, cables, and photographs of Roosevelt's letters to the sultan, and concludes Roosevelt did make supportive statements which the US then denied. FRUS is where to check that directly.
access: Free and fully online.

fonds: Colonial administration and personnel; Algerian series bearing on the Moroccan frontier and on Abd el-Kader's descendants.
holdings: The French colonial administrative record, including Algeria — which matters because the Moroccan frontier, the Touat question and the Abd el-Kader family thread all run through Algiers.
whatItCanSettle: The Algerian-Moroccan frontier disputes; the Touat annexation of 1901; the surveillance of Emir Abd el-Malek, whose family France had exiled from Algeria.
access: Reading room; substantial online finding aids and some digitised material.

institution: League of Nations Archives / UN Geneva
fonds: League of Nations Secretariat files; mandates and petitions series; press cuttings.
holdings: Petitions, correspondence and press material relating to colonial North Africa. Shakib Arslan operated from Geneva and used the League's environment to internationalise the 1930 Berber dahir campaign.
whatItCanSettle: How the Moroccan nationalist case was made internationally before 1945; Arslan's networks; the reception of the dahir campaign outside Morocco. Morocco was a protectorate, not a mandate, so it is not in the mandates system — but the Geneva milieu is where its case was argued.
access: Reading room; substantial digitisation under the Total Digital Access project.

institution: Tangier American Legation Institute for Moroccan Studies (TALIM)
fonds: Legation building archive, library and museum collections.
holdings: The oldest US diplomatic property abroad, gifted by Sultan Moulay Suleiman. Material on the American presence at Tangier, the Perdicaris affair, and the international zone.
whatItCanSettle: The Perdicaris affair from the legation's own records — minister Samuel Gummere was the man on the spot for the 'Perdicaris alive or Raisuli dead' episode. Also the social history of the Tangier international zone.
access: Museum and research library, Tangier.

institution: Instance Équité et Réconciliation (IER) — final report and archive
fonds: Final report (2005–06), testimony records, reparations files. Related holdings at the Conseil National des Droits de l'Homme.
holdings: The Moroccan state's own investigation into the Years of Lead: disappearances, arbitrary detention, deaths in custody, and the repression of the Rif in 1958–59 and of the 1965, 1981 and 1984 risings.
whatItCanSettle: The strongest available OFFICIAL source for Phase IX — a state documenting its own violence. Use it as a floor, not a ceiling: it was a negotiated process that named few individuals and did not pursue criminal accountability, and Human Rights Watch published a critical assessment in 2005.
access: Report published and widely available; underlying testimony records restricted.

fonds: Alaouite dynastic records
holdings: ʿAlawite dynasty records, including correspondence between the sultan and his governors — precisely the material that would show how the Makhzen actually managed tribes and qaids.
whatItCanSettle: The nature of the appointments that this workspace treats as disputed: Mouha ou Hammou's qaid commission, Ma al-'Aynayn's Saharan khalifate, the terms on which sultans dealt with tribal power. The conditional bay'a of 1908 may also be here.
access: Palace library; access restricted and by permission.

institution: Archives diplomatiques — La Courneuve and Nantes
fonds: Correspondance politique / Maroc; Traités; at Nantes, Protectorat Maroc — Résidence Générale, Direction des Affaires Indigènes, and the post archives for Tangier and the consulates.
holdings: French diplomatic correspondence and the civil administration of the Protectorate, as distinct from its military record.
whatItCanSettle: Regnault's reporting of 29–31 March 1912; the Résidence–Paris correspondence of May–August 1953; the Algeciras and 1904 loan files; the signed French instrument of the Treaty of Fez.
access: Reading rooms; finding aids published online as PDFs.

fonds: Digitised out-of-copyright monographs and periodicals.
holdings: Contemporary French and English works on Morocco. Confirmed present: Ch. René-Leclerc / Georges type works (La France au Maroc), Chérif Ouazzani-era material, Sségonzac's Au cœur de l'Atlas, Le Maroc artistique, a Moulay Youssef and Lyautey item dated 1912, and an item indexed as 'bataille elhri'.
whatItCanSettle: The workable substitute for Gallica when its search fails. These are PRIMARY_CONTEMPORARY texts, readable now, at no cost. The next research session should exploit this before anything else.
access: Free and fully online.

institution: Archivio Storico Diplomatico — Ministero degli Affari Esteri
fonds: Serie politica; Documenti diplomatici italiani. Also Archivio Centrale dello Stato, Ministero delle Colonie, Trattati ed accordi internazionali in materia coloniale.
holdings: Italian diplomatic correspondence bearing on the North African settlement.
whatItCanSettle: The Franco-Italian accords of 1900–1902, in which France conceded Italian claims in Tripolitania in exchange for Italian acquiescence in Morocco. Morocco was traded for Libya in a bilateral bargain no Moroccan participated in — the same mechanism as the 1904 Entente and the 1911 Franco-German convention, and the least examined of the three. Italy also supplied military instructors and assisted at Dar al-Makina.
access: Reading room, Rome; the Documenti diplomatici italiani series is published.

institution: Bibliothèque Nationale du Royaume du Maroc (BNRM)
fonds: Manuscripts; historical periodicals; digitised collections
holdings: Large Arabic manuscript collections and historical periodicals, including the nationalist and Protectorate-era press.
whatItCanSettle: The Moroccan press record of the nationalist period; the Arabic textual tradition; possibly Ma al-'Aynayn's own writings, which this workspace currently substitutes European reports for.
access: Public library with an online catalogue — unusually, better catalogued online than Archives du Maroc.
